born.why: The code prioritizes survival by treating any previous poisoning instance of the same species as absolute poison, switching to 'leave' unless starving; it uses 'taste' for novel species to gather data with minimal risk, and only commits to 'eat' when historical data indicates a high safety margin (>70% safe), ensuring long-term health over immediate gratification.

The code prioritizes survival by eating only when starving, uses trait-similarity to infer safety from past diary entries (avoiding fruits similar to poisonous ones), and distinguishes between carrying known good fruits for later versus eating immediately based on current hunger levels.

The code prioritizes survival by eating only when critically hungry, avoids fruits matching known poison traits via smell/color/shape heuristics, and uses 'taste' for safe learning of new species while preferring to carry home identified target fruits.

The code prioritizes survival by eating when starving (>95%), avoids known poisons, efficiently carries known safe food unless hungry, and cautiously tastes unknown fruits only when hunger is manageable (<80) to minimize death risk from poisoning.

The code prioritizes survival by avoiding fruits with traits shared with previously poisoned ones, uses a similarity-based value system to prefer known-safe species, and only eats/tastes when hunger is significant or the fruit appears promising, while carrying home specific target fruits if they are deemed safe.
